maya: Drafting a short runbook for 'spot fallback routing + cost guardrails' — aiming for clear drain steps, automated fallback triggers, and what the escalation path looks like. Putting a draft here, pls poke holes. :speech_balloon:

ben: Love it. Two quick asks: include the exact metric thresholds for the guardrail, and a one-line customer-facing notification template.

jamie: Adding: we should separate graceful-drain vs force-evict flows. Graceful tries to finish running jobs, force evict kills and reschedules.

maya: Agreed. Draft below. Feedback welcome.

maya: RUNBOOK (draft):
1) Trigger conditions (automated):
   - Spot preemption rate > 10% over 5m AND available spot capacity < 15% of pool size -> start fallback evaluation.
   - Average tail latency (p95) > 1.2x baseline for 3m AND queue depth rising -> consider immediate fallback.
   - Manual trigger: on-call runs `infra fallback start --pool gpu-spot-us-west`

2) Pre-fallback checks (automated, fail-open warnings):
   - Check running jobs: `kubectl get pods -l pool=gpu-spot -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'`
   - Check active allocations and estimated restart cost. If > $X/day then alert FinOps.

3) Graceful drain sequence (preferred):
   - Set pool to draining: tag nodes `drain=true` and set max-surge=0.
   - Notify scheduler: `api: /pools/gpu-spot/actions?op=drain` (internal)
   - Wait up to 10m for in-flight requests to finish, then move new traffic to fallback route.

4) Force-evict sequence (if grace fails or emergency):
   - Cord on nodes and `kubectl delete pods --grace-period=30 --force` with reroute enforcement.
   - If preemptions continue while draining, escalate to Ops lead.

5) Fallback routing and cost guardrail enforcement:
   - Primary fallback: shift traffic to reserved/dedicated capacity in same region.
   - Secondary fallback: route to on-demand cheapest-region pool if cross-region allowed.
   - Cost guardrail check before secondary fallback: query `cost_delta = projected_hourly_cost(new_route) - current_hourly_cost`. If cost_delta > $200/h, block auto-secondary fallback and send approval request to #finance-ops and oncall.
   - We implement a soft cap: automatic secondary fallback allowed up to +$50/h without approval; above that requires manual approval.

6) Customer-facing notification template (one-line + link):
   - "Heads up: We’re routing requests to alternative capacity due to temporary GPU spot shortages. You may see slight latency changes. Details: <link-to-status-page>"

7) Metrics & dashboards to monitor during fallback:
   - spot_preempt_rate, pool_available_pct, p95_latency, cost_delta, reroute_success_rate, sla_error_rate

8) Escalation path:
   - On-call tries mitigations (10m), if unresolved -> page Ops lead -> if cost > guardrail threshold page FinOps -> Exec ops if customer SLA impacted.

9) Post-mortem checklist (after normalizing):
   - Capture timestamps of trigger, routing changes, cost delta, and final resolution.
   - Update pool sizing or autoscaler config if this repeats > 3 times in 7d.

sam: A few concrete details to add: where exactly do we store the guardrail values? I'd like them in configstore under `infra.guardrails.spot_fallback` so we can change without deploy.

maya: Good call. I'll add param names and default values.

maya: PARAMS (proposal):
- infra.guardrails.spot_preempt_rate_pct = 10
- infra.guardrails.pool_available_pct = 15
- infra.guardrails.p95_multiplier = 1.2
- infra.guardrails.secondary_cost_soft_cap = 50  # USD per hour
- infra.guardrails.secondary_cost_hard_cap = 200 # USD per hour

infra-bot: autoscaler: detected spot_preempt_rate=12.4% for gpu-spot-us-west, available_pct=9% -> entering fallback-eval state (1790001205)

ben: infra-bot hit looks real. Add runbook step: if autoscaler enters fallback-eval, set a temporary maintenance window in the console so customers see the banner. Command: `infra ui maintenance create --pool gpu-spot-us-west --reason "spot capacity low" --duration 60m`

nora: For cross-region fallback: make sure KMS keys are allowed in target region and we don't violate data residency. Add a mandatory residency-check step before switching region.

oncall: Also add a quick rollback command if cost explodes during fallback: `infra fallback rollback --point-in-time <ts>` — that should revert routing to the last stable config and alert the team.

jamie: Suggestion: add a short decision tree image later, but the text steps suffice for now.
